content.text:
This is not a website-login failure. The crash happens before any browser/site login:

`__main__ → plan_assignments → model.complete → QWEN APIConnectionError`

I confirmed nothing is listening at the documented local proxy address `127.0.0.1:8765`. Your Qwen proxy is not running (or has stopped), while the runner still has a `QWEN_BASE_URL` pointing at it.

Start/restart it in a separate terminal and keep it open:

```sh
atira models proxy
```

Then ensure the terminal that runs the agent has the exports printed by that command (especially `QWEN_BASE_URL` and `QWEN_API_KEY`), then rerun:

```sh
eval "$(atira scout --challenge rfq --env)"
uv run --no-sync python -m rfq_agent
```

Also update the model identifier in `src/rfq_agent/model.py` from:

```python
QWEN_MODEL = "qwen3.8-flash-next"
```

to the currently documented proxy alias:

```python
QWEN_MODEL = "qwen"
```

The local README already correctly requires the model proxy, but the command sequence you showed only refreshes scouting credentials; it does not start or repair the proxy. The official docs likewise specify that local Qwen calls go through `atira models proxy`.

I reviewed the challenge, RFQ rules, fair-play policy, README, architecture spec, and source. Your dynamic browser/model-directed approach is aligned with the rules; no repository files were changed.

Your `/status` shows **Free** and only **4% of the monthly limit** remains, resetting **November 9 at 13:45**. The $70 promotion may still help with Codex, but first check what kind of credit it is:

1. Open [ChatGPT Usage](https://chatgpt.com/settings/usage) while signed into **vlad.moroshan@gmail.com**.
2. Look for the **Codex/usage credit balance** and recent credit history. If the $70 is a ChatGPT usage-credit balance, it should apply to eligible Codex usage after your included allowance is used; there’s no separate code to enter in Codex.
3. If it appears only as a **wallet balance** or **API credit**, it won’t automatically pay for Codex usage. ChatGPT usage credits and wallet funds are separate, and ChatGPT usage credits are not API credits. [OpenAI’s credit guide](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12642688-using-credits-for-flexible-usage-in-chatgpt-personal-plans)

Because your account is Free, the credits article says credit purchases are only available to some Free accounts, though an existing eligible balance may still be usable. Check the Usage page for the balance and whether it lists Codex as supported. [OpenAI’s Codex usage guidance](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11369540-using-codex-with-your-chatgpt-plan)

If the $70 doesn’t show as Codex usage credits there, contact OpenAI Support from the Help Center chat and include the promotion code privately, the date it was applied, a screenshot of `/status`, and the Usage page. Don’t share the code publicly.
